result.topic_en: The page first finishes a calculus-of-variations remark about an endpoint constrained to a surface and the independence theorem. It then asks whether a definite ternary form of even order can be written as a sum of positive even powers of linear forms, linking this to the sign of the 'Kanonisante' and to the stability of such representations under small perturbations.

items.english: Whether a, say, ternary form of even order that is definite can be represented as a sum of positive powers of linear forms is probably simply tied to whether the Kanonisante turns out positive.

items.quote:
Im Fall der definiten Formen giebt es nun nur 2
Unterfälle, der durch positive $2n^{te}$ Potenzen darstellbaren und der nicht
so darstellbaren Formen; wenigstens kann man die darstellbaren alle kon-
tinuirlich in einander überführen.
items.english: In the case of definite forms there are now only 2 subcases: the forms representable by positive 2n-th powers and the forms not so representable; at least one can transform all the representable ones continuously into one another.

items.english: If I take a form representable by positive powers whose Kanonisante does not vanish, then certainly every form lying in a sufficiently small neighbourhood of it is likewise representable by positive powers.
